title: Design URL Shortener (Bitly)
requirements: Given a long URL, return a much shorter unique alias.
When users access a short URL, they should be redirected to the original link.
High availability and low latency redirects.
Links expire after a standard default timespan.
Analytics: How many times a redirection happened?
capacityEstimation:
Traffic: 100M new URLs generated per month.
Read/Write ratio: 100:1. So 10B redirects per month.
QPS: Writes = 40/s, Reads = 4000/s.
Storage: 100M * 100 months * 500 bytes = 5TB.
highLevelDesign:
1. API Gateway routes traffic.
2. URL Shortening Service generates base62 hashes (using a counter or UUID approach).
3. Redirection Service looks up the short URL in cache/DB and issues HTTP 301.
4. Database stores Short -> Long mapping.
5. Analytics system ingests click events.
tradeoffs: HTTP 301 vs 302: 301 (Permanent) caches the redirect in the browser, saving server load. 302 (Temporary) allows better analytics since every click hits our server.
Hashing vs Counter: MD5 hashing can have collisions. A distributed counter (e.g., ZooKeeper or Snowflake) generating a unique ID and then converting to Base62 avoids collisions entirely.
databaseChoice:
NoSQL (like Cassandra or DynamoDB) or RDBMS (PostgreSQL).
Since the schema is simple (ShortUrl -> LongUrl) and read-heavy, NoSQL is excellent for high scale, but RDBMS is perfectly fine since the total data size is manageable (5TB) and we can heavily rely on caching.
cachingStrategy: Memcached or Redis. Cache the most frequently accessed short URLs. Eviction policy: LRU (Least Recently Used). Since the read/write ratio is 100:1, caching will drastically reduce DB load.
description: Design a URL shortening service like Bitly. The system should generate unique aliases for long URLs and efficiently redirect users who access the short URLs, while handling billions of requests per month.
